problem: Heading altered beyond title case: 'Which' to 'That', 'Avidity' to 'The eagerness'.
replacement: Accidental or Providential Causes Which Contribute to the Maintenance of the Democratic Republic in the United States The Union has no neighbors—No metropolis—The Americans have had the chances of birth in their favor—America an empty country—How this circumstance contributes powerfully to the maintenance of the democratic republic in America—How the American wilds are peopled—Avidity of the Anglo-Americans in taking possession of the solitudes of the New World—Influence of physical prosperity on the political opinions of the Americans.

America has no great capital city *a whose influence is felt, directly or indirectly, over the whole country. I consider this one of the chief causes of the survival of republican institutions in the United States. In cities it is impossible to prevent people from gathering and stirring one another into sudden and passionate resolutions. Cities may be regarded as large assemblies in which every inhabitant is a member. Their populace has an enormous influence on the magistrates, and often carries out its own wishes without their involvement.

problem: Causal 'As inhabitants of a country where they have no civil rights' became a bare coordinate statement, losing the reason.
replacement: a [ The United States has no metropolis, but it already contains several very large cities. In 1830 Philadelphia counted 161,000 inhabitants and New York 202,000. The lower classes who live in these cities form a rabble even more dangerous than the populace of European towns. They consist, first, of freed Black people, whom the laws and public opinion condemn to a hereditary state of misery and degradation. They also include a multitude of Europeans who have been driven to the shores of the New World by misfortune or misconduct. These men infect the United States with all our vices, and they bring with them none of the interests that might counteract their harmful influence. Because they live in a country where they have no civil rights, they are ready to turn every passion that stirs the community to their own advantage. Thus, within the last few months, serious riots have broken out in Philadelphia and in New York. Disturbances of this kind are unknown in the rest of the country, which is not at all alarmed by them, because the city population has so far had no power or influence over the rural districts. Nevertheless, I regard the size of certain American cities, and especially the nature of their population, as a real danger to the future security of the democratic republics of the New World. I venture to predict that they will perish from this cause, unless the government manages to create an armed force that will stay under the control of the national majority while remaining independent of the city population and able to put down its excesses.

problem: Awkward relative clause 'The pioneers follow, who cut through...'.
replacement: That continent still shows, as it did in the earliest times, rivers that rise from never-failing sources, green and moist solitudes, and fields that the farmer’s plow has never turned. In this state it is offered to man. It is offered not to man in the barbarous and isolated condition of the early ages, but to a being who already holds the most powerful secrets of the natural world, who is united with his fellow men, and who has been instructed by the experience of fifty centuries. At this very moment thirteen million civilized Europeans are peacefully spreading over those fertile plains, whose resources and extent they do not yet know accurately themselves. Three or four thousand soldiers drive the wandering Native American tribes before them. The pioneers follow the soldiers. They cut through the woods, scare off the beasts of prey, trace the courses of the inland streams, and prepare the triumphal march of civilization across the wilderness.
Three principal causes of the maintenance of the democratic republic—Federal Constitutions—Municipal institutions—Judicial power.

problem: 'free exercise of their own privileges' lost its noun, leaving 'of their own'.
replacement: But as soon as the priesthood is entirely separated from the government, as it is in the United States, no class of men is found more naturally disposed than the Catholics to carry the doctrine of the equality of conditions into the political world. If, then, the Catholic citizens of the United States are not forcibly led by the nature of their beliefs to adopt democratic and republican principles, at least they are not necessarily opposed to them. And their social position, as well as their small numbers, obliges them to adopt these opinions. Most of the Catholics are poor, and they have no chance of taking part in the government unless it is open to all citizens. They are a minority, and all rights must be respected in order to secure them the free exercise of their own privileges. These two causes lead them, without their knowing it, to adopt political doctrines that they would perhaps support with less zeal if they were rich and dominant.
